reports.title: EARNINGS RELEASE FOR THE QUARTER ENDED SEPTEMBER 30, 2026

desk.headline: Revenue up 22% to a record $4.57bn on World Cup and political ads; adjusted EPS $2.54 beat $2.12 estimate; no formal guidance
results: Record first-quarter revenue and Adjusted EBITDA. Advertising jumped 47% on the FIFA Men's World Cup, more political ads and Tubi growth.
Television segment revenue rose 32% to $2.71bn and its EBITDA more than doubled to $934m. Cable networks revenue rose 8% to $1.80bn.
Net income attributable to stockholders was $943m ($2.20 a share), up from $599m. Higher sports rights and World Cup production costs pushed expenses up.
Operating cash flow was $616m, against an outflow of $130m a year earlier. Cash was $4.54bn and borrowings $6.61bn at 30 September.
No shares were bought back in the quarter (a year earlier: $250m). Dividends and distributions paid came to $131m.

guidance.summary: Fox gives no numerical guidance in its release. On the call, management said it expects full-year buybacks within its usual range, resuming this quarter.

points: Management credited the World Cup, strong NFL and college football starts, and a record midterm political ad cycle for the quarter.
Tubi revenue grew about 35%, and growth carried into the current quarter. The CEO sees Tubi margins eventually around 20%.
Fox One subscribers are almost entirely new to Fox, but the CEO warned growth may be seasonal and won't always offset pay-TV losses.
The CEO put a dip in Fox News ratings down to viewer "fatigue", not viewers switching away.
The Roku deal has shareholder and foreign approvals; Fox is working with the US DOJ on clearance and took no deal questions.
call.source: TheWrap and MarketBeat coverage of the 2 Nov 2026 results call
